query: For automotive exhaust catalysts, what single intervention could improve catalytic activity and durability while reducing platinum-group-metal consumption? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment with a clear outcome that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of a Cu-Ce bimetallic system into a Ba0.7MnO3 perovskite catalyst will improve its catalytic activity and durability for CO oxidation while reducing platinum-group-metal consumption.
generation.intervention: Introduction of a Cu-Ce bimetallic system
generation.conditions: Conditions similar to those found in the exhaust of last-generation automotive internal combustion engines
generation.mechanism: The Cu-Ce bimetallic system improves the redox properties and increases the proportion of reduced copper species on the surface, leading to enhanced catalytic activity
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved CO conversion at low temperatures and increased tolerance to CO2
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism of the Cu-Ce bimetallic system's effect on the catalyst's performance is not fully understood

falsification_experiment.design: Temperature-Programmed Reduction with H2 (H2-TPR) and O2 Temperature-Programmed Desorption (O2-TPD) tests
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Cu-Ce bimetallic system does not improve the catalytic activity and durability of the Ba0.7MnO3 perovskite catalyst, as evidenced by no significant increase in CO conversion and no change in H2 consumption and O2 desorption, then the hypothesis is falsified

## Abstract
AbstractTwo copper-containing perovskites Ba0.8Mn0.7Cu0.3O3 and Cu(4 wt%)/Ba0.7MnO3 (selected from previous studies) were tested as catalysts for the CO oxidation reaction under conditions similar to the found in the exhaust of last-generation automotive internal combustion engines. The Cu(4 wt%)/Ba0.7MnO3 sample has been selected due to its higher tolerance to CO2. In order to optimize the performance of this sample for the reaction under study, a Cu(2 wt%)Ce(2 wt%)/Ba0.7MnO3 formulation was synthesized, characterized and tested. The excellent catalytic performance of the bimetallic formulation, in terms of CO conversion at low temperatures and tolerance to CO2, is because cerium improves the redox properties and increases the proportion of reduced copper species on the surface compared to the Cu(4 wt%)/Ba0.7MnO3 sample.Keywords: perovskite, manganese, copper, cerium, CO oxidation

It is, therefore, easy to understand that the development of new catalytic systems that combine high efficiency with lower use of PGMs is a challenge for the research community, both for environmental and economic reasons [].
An ideal new catalyst would be one that could combine high reactivity with one metal or a combination of metals characterized by high physical abundance and low cost. Copper, which has been increasingly used in catalytic applications over the last two decades, could be regarded as a proper candidate. The high natural abundance of copper, compared with precious metals, the interesting applications in organic synthesis (e.g., Gilman reagents or as co-catalyst in Sonogashira reaction) and its catalytic properties, is an attractive background [,,].
